title: Guest Room Security & Privacy
blurb: Keeping guest rooms secure and guests' privacy respected: keys, verifying guests, knocking and discretion.
siteNotes: How master keys are signed out and kept secure.
How a guest is verified when someone asks to be let in.
Which manager to report concerning finds to, including out of hours.
legalNotes: CHECK: the trainer says to report weapons, drugs or signs a guest may be vulnerable to your manager, who will decide what to do. Confirm the venue's procedure, including when to call 999 or the police straight away, and the safeguarding route for a vulnerable guest.
Guest privacy is also a data protection point (UK GDPR); not quoted on slides.

cards.title: Guest Room Security & Privacy
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- keep keys and keycards secure
- verify a guest before letting anyone in a room
- respect privacy and report concerns

cards.title: Guests trust us with their space
cards.body:
Guests trust us with their private space and their belongings, and protecting that trust is a core part of the job.

It comes down to two things: keeping rooms secure, and respecting guests' privacy.

cards.title: Keys come first
cards.body:
Never lend your keys or keycards, never leave them lying around, and keep master keys especially secure.

Never let anyone into a guest's room unless you have verified they are the guest staying there. A polite check protects everyone. Never tell anyone a guest's room number or confirm who is staying.

cards.body: Always knock and announce yourself before entering a room, and respect "do not disturb" signs.

items.title: Enter
items.text: Only when it is right to

cards.title: Private means private
cards.body:
Do not touch or move guests' belongings any more than the job needs, and never look through, borrow or comment on their possessions.

What you see in a room stays private. Do not discuss or share it, and never on social media.

left.title: Do
items: Touch belongings only as the job needs

right.title: Do not
items: Post about them on social media

cards.title: Report what concerns you
cards.body:
If you come across something concerning in a room, do not ignore it. Report it to your manager, who will decide what to do.

Respect and discretion are what make guests feel safe with us.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Never lend or leave keys or keycards; keep master keys especially secure.
- Verify the guest before letting anyone into a room.
- Never share a room number or confirm who is staying.
- Knock and announce yourself, and respect "do not disturb" signs.
- What you see in a room stays private. Report concerns to your manager.

cards.q: You should never tell anyone a guest's room number.
cards.why: Never tell anyone a guest's room number or confirm who is staying.

cards.q: What should you do before entering a guest's room?
options: Check the minibar before you start
Use the master key straight away
Open the door a little and listen in
cards.why: Always knock and announce yourself before entering, and respect "do not disturb" signs.

cards.q: You should let someone into a guest's room…
options: Only once you have verified they are the guest
If they ask nicely and say it is urgent
If they say they have lost their own key
If they can tell you the room number
cards.why: Never let anyone in unless you have verified they are the guest staying there.

cards.q: You should respect "do not disturb" signs.
cards.why: Always respect "do not disturb" signs, and knock and announce yourself before entering.

cards.q: It is fine to look through or comment on a guest's belongings.
cards.why: Never look through, borrow or comment on guests' possessions.

cards.q: What you see in a guest's room should be…
cards.why: What you see in a room stays private. Do not discuss or share it, and definitely never on social media.

cards.q: If you find something concerning in a room, such as weapons or a vulnerable guest, what do you do?
options: Ask the guest about it directly
Say nothing to avoid a fuss
cards.why: Do not ignore it. Report it to your manager, who will decide what to do.

cards.q: Master keys should be kept especially secure.
cards.why: Keep master keys especially secure. Never lend keys or leave them lying around.

cards.q: You can discuss guests' private details on social media.
cards.why: What you see in a room stays private, and definitely never on social media.

cards.q: Protecting guests' rooms comes down to security and…
cards.why: Protecting guests' rooms comes down to two things: keeping rooms secure, and respecting guests' privacy.
